name: CA-01
label: Likely D

key_factors: Post-redistricting district leans Democratic by seven points in a favorable Democratic environment
Prediction markets price McGuire near 95% despite the Republican incumbent
McGuire outraised Gallagher and has outside backing, though Gallagher holds more cash on hand
No public polls or expert ratings, so fundamentals carry the forecast
model.rationale: The redrawn district leans seven points Democratic and the year's environment compounds that edge, with prediction markets aligning behind McGuire at about 95 percent. Gallagher's incumbency and cash advantage are real but unlikely to close a double-digit structural gap, so this sits just below the safe threshold.
model.watch: New polling or a surge of outside spending showing Gallagher running near even with the district's partisan lean would turn this into a genuine contest.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; fundamentals point clearly one way (post-redistricting), so it is treated as safe for that party.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
California's first district became considerably more Democratic after redistricting, and Republican incumbent James Gallagher now defends a seat that leans seven points toward the Democrats. No public polling is available, but prediction markets give Democrat Mike McGuire roughly a 95 percent chance of winning, and the political environment this year favors Democrats in California.

Money is competitive: McGuire has raised about $1.8 million with more than $600,000 in outside support, while Gallagher has brought in about $1.5 million and holds the edge in cash on hand. Incumbency gives Gallagher a modest cushion, but he starts well behind the district's partisan lean in an unfavorable year. The race rates as Likely Democratic, with Gallagher needing to run well ahead of his party's baseline to survive.
